svg.title: limit-handoff simulate demo
svg.desc: Terminal output of limit-handoff simulate on a sample chat: it writes a cut-off block in HANDOFF.md, a recovered context file and a paste prompt that names the next step.
svg.text: ~/code/store — real output of limit-handoff 1.0.0 (temp path shortened)

g.text: $ limit-handoff simulate --dir ~/code/store
Simulated a StopFailure (rate_limit) with session id simulated-20261101-131118-56206 in
~/code/store.
HANDOFF.md: cut-off block added (~/code/store/HANDOFF.md)
Paste prompt: ~/code/store/PASTE-PROMPT.txt
Recovered context: ~/code/store/.handoff/recovered-20261101-131119-simulate.md
$ grep -A3 "^## Next steps" HANDOFF.md; grep "^>" HANDOFF.md
## Next steps (in order)
1. Add email and password validation
2. Match the login page error style
3. Write a test for the form
> ⚠️ **Session cut off** (usage limit reached — 5-hour limit, resets Sun 01 Nov 15:41 GMT)
at 2026-11-01 13:11. The steps above may be slightly behind.
> Check the files for a half-finished step before continuing. Recovered context:
`.handoff/recovered-20261101-131119-simulate.md`
$ cat PASTE-PROMPT.txt
Continue my task in ~/code/store. My last chat stopped (usage limit reached — 5-hour limit,
resets Sun 01 Nov 15:41 GMT). First read ~/code/store/HANDOFF.md fully — it has the goal,
what is done, decisions, and the exact next steps. Then read
~/code/store/.handoff/recovered-20261101-131119-simulate.md for the last messages before
the cut-off. Check the files for any half-finished step, then start with: Add email and
password validation. Do not redo finished steps. Keep HANDOFF.md updated as you work.
